title: Marco Polo on the Silk Road
description: 1271-1275. Escort the young Marco Polo, his father Niccolo, and their trade caravan across the deserts and mountain passes of Central Asia to the court of Kublai Khan. Bandit raiders and harsh terrain threaten the route; the caravan's pack animals must survive. Victory requires bringing Marco alive to the Khan's summer palace at Shangdu.

anachronisms_found: EL_CID (Rodrigo Diaz, died 1099, Castile) placed as a caravan figure - wrong century and wrong region by nearly two hundred years; he is used to stand in for a 13th-century Venetian merchant
WILLIAM_THE_CONQUEROR (died 1087, Normandy/England) placed in the Polo caravan - an 11th-century Norman king has no business on the 1271 Silk Road
GENGHIS_KHAN placed as a GAIA object at the destination: Genghis died in 1227 and the Polos were received by his grandson Kublai Khan, whose hero unit exists in the editor and should have been used
KNIGHT x3 as caravan escort - heavy Latin-Christian shock cavalry crossing Persia and the Pamirs is implausible; camel riders or light cavalry escorts were available in the engine
SHEEP x6 standing in for the caravan's pack animals when TRADE_CART and camel units were available and far more representative of a Silk Road caravan
CASTLE/KEEP used to represent Shangdu, giving the Khan's summer palace generic European stone-fortress architecture; a Wonder or pagoda-style structure would have read better

issues_found: Marco Polo is represented by the WILLIAM_THE_CONQUEROR hero unit — a named eleventh-century Norman standing in for a thirteenth-century Venetian; the victory and defeat triggers key off him by that name, so the substitution is structural, not cosmetic. Renaming a generic unit was available.
Niccolo Polo is represented by the EL_CID hero — an eleventh-century Castilian, again a named figure from the wrong century and culture.

GENGHIS_KHAN is placed at the destination as the Khan the caravan is travelling to meet, but the Polos were received by Kublai Khan; Genghis died in 1227, 44 years before the journey's start. The engine ships no Kublai hero, so a renamed generic (or the Khan of the Mongol civ) was the correct fallback.
Both active players are left as civilization RANDOM, so architecture set, unit roster and language are unassigned — Shangdu may be rendered in Teutonic or Frankish stonework at random.

Shangdu is built from a CASTLE and two KEEPs, European fortification models rather than anything suggesting the Khan's summer palace; a walled compound of Mongol/Chinese-flavoured buildings was possible.

The escort is CROSSBOWMAN and KNIGHT — Western European heavy cavalry and crossbows for a merchant caravan that in fact travelled with local guides, camels and Mongol-issued safe-conduct; camels or trade carts existed in the catalogue.
Pack animals are modelled as SHEEP, which are herdable food rather than laden beasts; trade carts or camels would have carried the 'caravan goods' idea the defeat text asserts.

Marco Polo is represented by the WILLIAM_THE_CONQUEROR hero — an 11th-century Norman duke standing in for a 13th-century Venetian teenager; a renamed generic villager/trade cart/militia would have been the correct abstraction, so this is avoidable cross-culture, cross-century casting.
Niccolo Polo is represented by EL_CID, an 11th-century Castilian warlord — again a wrong-culture, wrong-era hero model where a renamed generic unit was available.
GENGHIS_KHAN is placed (in GAIA) to stand for Kublai Khan at Shangdu; right culture but the wrong Khan, dead 44 years before the scenario's arrival date.

Both players' civilizations are left RANDOM, so architecture for the Venetian caravan, the bandit camp and Shangdu is undefined — no Chinese or Central Asian architecture set is guaranteed, and Shangdu itself is rendered only as a Castle plus two Keeps.

The escort is composed of KNIGHTs and CROSSBOWMEN — a European men-at-arms escort rather than the hired local guides and guards a Venetian merchant caravan would have used across Persia and the Pamir.
The bandit force is entirely mounted (cavalry archers, light cavalry, scouts) plus an ARCHERY_RANGE, giving raiders a permanent military production building rather than a camp.
The 'Defeat Caravan Lost' condition counts player 1 objects across the whole 120x120 map rather than the pack animals specifically, so its parameters do not actually track the sheep it claims to.
